title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Opus 5 ships today — watch item confirmed, headline feature is the effort toggle (Jul 24)
bullets.summary: Opus 5 is live on all Anthropic platforms at $5/$25 per 1M (unchanged from Opus 4.8), nears Fable 5's frontier intelligence at ~half the price, becomes the new default on Claude Max, and ships with a low/medium/high effort toggle plus a Fast mode (~2.5x speed at 2x price). Internal Frontier-Bench v0.1 runs more than double Opus 4.8 at lower cost per task.
bullets.how: Single most important item for The Construct: the whole fleet can run at Opus quality with a per-job effort dial we control directly rather than swapping models. Benchmark coding + computer-use agents on Opus 5 and set default effort tiers per job class this week.

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless spec is now 4 days out — the breaking rewrite ratifies Tuesday
bullets.summary: The stateless core (no session id, any request to any instance, OAuth-aligned auth, formal deprecation policy) plus MCP Apps (server-rendered UI) and the Tasks extension ratify Jul 28; beta SDKs are already shipping.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is 4 days from a breaking change; close the migration inventory + hardening checklist before Tuesday. The Tasks extension maps directly onto our long-running scan jobs. Load-bearing action of the week.

bullets.title: Claude Developer Platform — Managed Agents gain model-effort settings, expanded webhooks, and session seeding (July)
bullets.summary: You can set an effort level on a Managed Agents model config, get webhook coverage for environment + memory-store events, seed a session with initial events, and add optional version checks on updates.
bullets.how: API-side twin of the Opus 5 effort toggle: dial effort (cost/quality) per job programmatically, wire memory/env events into our dashboards, and seed context so scan agents start warm instead of cold.

bullets.title: Anthropic upgrades Claude voice mode — Sonnet/Opus + reasoning, no longer hard-wired to Haiku (Jul 23)
bullets.summary: Paid users can switch between Haiku/Sonnet/Opus mid-conversation and the model can think through hard problems out loud; free accounts stay on a single Haiku connection.
bullets.how: Makes hands-free operation of a Construct agent viable for real work (dictated triage, on-the-go strategy) instead of only quick lookups; useful for Bobby's mobile workflow, less so for headless jobs.

bullets.title: Revid.ai launches an MCP server + CLI for end-to-end AI video production (Jul 16)
bullets.summary: Stable-named tools (render_video, clone_voice, schedule_publish, publish_now) let an agent run script -> render -> voiceover -> caption -> publish in one call across nine workflows, with OAuth 2.1 for hosted clients.
bullets.how: Closest off-the-shelf analog to a Brand 9 Signs creative-ops pipeline: one Construct agent turns a signage brief into finished motion/spot assets and schedules the post, no editor in the loop.

praxis_lesson: The per-call effort-control thesis this board has carried all week is now fully realized in a shipped flagship: Claude Opus 5's headline feature is a low/medium/high effort toggle (mirrored by Managed Agents' effort setting and voice mode's tier inheritance), so the operating discipline is no longer 'which model' but 'govern how much effort each job is allowed to spend' — and that lever now runs at Opus quality across the whole fleet. Load-bearing move stays the Jul-28 stateless-MCP migration + hardening inventory (4 days out), with least-authority scoping on every new write-capable connector as the standing governance hook. The Opus 5 watch item, open since Jul 23, is now closed/confirmed.
